title: Colour Mixing Lab
strapline: Blue and yellow in a pot, a stir, and — green! Making brand-new colours you've never seen before.
intent: Mixing colours is a small piece of magic children can cause themselves — two colours meet and a new one appears — and that wonder drives real investigation.
Predicting and testing what red and blue will make, then trying it, is genuine scientific enquiry with vivid, immediate results.
Pouring, dropping and stirring with pipettes, spoons and brushes builds fine-motor control and careful hand-eye coordination.
Naming and comparing the shades they create — darker, lighter, muddier, brighter — builds rich descriptive vocabulary.
Colour mixing is endlessly open-ended and no-fail, so every child can explore, invent and succeed at their own level.
It bridges science and art, feeding straight into painting, and helps children understand the colours in the world around them.
implementation: Offer the three primary colours in water, paint or ice, with pipettes, pots, spoons and white palettes or trays to mix on.
Ask for a prediction: 'what do you think blue and yellow will make?' — then let them mix it and see.
Celebrate the discoveries and the accidents: 'you made a brand-new colour — what shall we call it?'
Add clear pots and a light source so mixing colours in water glows, or freeze coloured ice cubes to melt and blend.
Model comparing words — 'that green is darker than this one, what did you add more of?'
Keep it exploratory; let children invent, name and remake colours rather than copying a chart.
key_questions: What do you think blue and yellow will make?
You made a brand-new colour — what shall we call it?
That green is darker than this one — what did you add more of?
How could we make this colour paler?
What happens if we mix all three together?

impact.text: Children predict, test and observe what colours make — genuine scientific enquiry with vivid results.
Children pour, drop and stir with pipettes, spoons and brushes, building fine-motor control.
Children make choices about colours and mix to see what happens.
Children name and compare the shades they create — darker, lighter, muddier, brighter.
Children invent, name and remake colours, owning a creation that is entirely theirs.

enhancements: Clear pots on a light source so mixed colours glow.
Coloured ice cubes to melt and blend into new shades.
The three primaries in water, paint and ice to explore across materials.
A colour-naming wall where children record and name their inventions.
A pipette-and-palette station for careful, controlled mixing.

playing_exploring: Children combine colours freely, delighting in each new shade they conjure.
Pipettes, pots and pools of colour invite endless, no-fail experimenting.
active_learning: Children pursue a colour they want — a particular green, a deep purple — and keep adjusting the mix to reach it.
creating_thinking: Children predict what two colours will make, test it, and work out what to add more of to change the result.
